# Davidek, Devaud, Robert & Blank 2005 — EXTRACTION
### *"The Effect of Reaction Conditions on the Origin and Yields of Acetic Acid Generated by the Maillard Reaction"*
### Glucose + glycine (0.1 M each) and the Amadori compound Fru-Gly (DFG), 0.2 M phosphate, pH 4 / 6 / 8, 120 °C, 0-240 min; 3-DG + glycine pH 4 / 6 / 8, 4 h; 13C-glucose isotopomers at 90 °C (15 h) and 120 °C (4 h), pH 6 / 8. Acetic acid by isotope dilution (SPME-GC-MS).

**Read 2026-10-31 from `data/articles/davidek2005.pdf`** (7 pp., Ann. N. Y. Acad. Sci. 1043:73-79; Acrobat Distiller
2005, clean text layer; the four figures are embedded 600 dpi 1-bit bitmaps, read from 200 / 400 / 800 dpi page
renders). This is the conference paper (Maillard symposium proceedings) that Davidek 2006a cites as ref 21 for the
Amadori-compound yields "about 4, 28, and 56 mol %"; it is the short preliminary report of the experiments that
Davidek 2006a then publishes in full. Much of its data reappears there (see section 5, duplicates).

**Legend.** **[V]** verbatim (short quote) · **[M]** number printed in this paper · **[F]** read off a figure by me ·
**[Q]** qualitative statement by the authors · **[C]** cited from another paper · **[Z]** derived by me, never printed ·
**[!]** flag.

## 1. What this paper answers for the model

Context: `results/validation/kinetic_core_dpo_partition_prereg.md` secs. 11-13. Davidek 2006a's amine-free 1-DG pots
exclude an amine-REQUIRED beta-cleavage; amine ACCELERATION is untested; arm B7a-2 tests a saturating pH law for the
DPO -> acetic acid cleavage.

| need | what Davidek 2005 gives | tag |
|---|---|---|
| (a) acetic / formic acid WITH vs WITHOUT amine, same precursor | **None.** Every pot contains glycine: glucose + glycine, 3-DG + glycine, and Fru-Gly, which carries glycine and releases it as it degrades (no free glycine added: "glucose and glycine were replaced by corresponding Amadori compound Fru-Gly"). Fru-Gly vs glucose + glycine is a precursor comparison (Amadori vs sugar + amine), not an amine on / off comparison. Formic acid only in the 3-DG + glycine pots | [M] / [Q] |
| (b) the DFG yields 4 / 28 / 56 mol % | **Fig. 1 end labels** (dotted lines, open markers) at **240 min, 120 °C, phosphate buffer, pH 4 / 6 / 8**; text: "at pH 8 the final yields of acetic acid from Fru-Gly and glucose/glycine were 56 mol% and 38 mol%". Method: acetic acid by IDA with [2H3]acetic acid, SPME (PDMS-DVB, 30 min 25 °C headspace) GC-MS, m/z 60 / 63. **The Methods never describe the Fru-Gly pots**: concentration, buffer strength and volume are not printed; 0.1 M Fru-Gly in 0.2 M phosphate, 0.4 mL vials is the natural reading of "replaced by" [Z, not printed]. Full time courses (my reads) in section 4 | [M] / [F] / [!] |
| (c) pH dependence | Glucose + glycine 240-min yields **1 / 17 / 38 mol %** and Fru-Gly **4 / 28 / 56 mol %** at pH 4 / 6 / 8 (end labels). Rise pH 6 -> 8: x2.2 (glucose), x2.0 (Fru-Gly); pH 4 -> 6: x17, x7 [Z]. Label origin (Fig. 4) changes little with pH: "The pH had only a negligible effect on the origin of acetic acid" [Q]. 3-DG + glycine acetic 0.8 / 1.5 / 2.4, formic 0.9 / 1.5 / 1.7 at pH 4 / 6 / 8 (Table 1; unit misprint, section 5) | [M] / [Z] |
| (d) isotope labelling | 13C-glucose + glycine: C-1/C-2 "about 67%" (120 °C, pH 8, Fig. 3), C-5/C-6 "about 20%", C-3/C-4 "<10%"; shares **constant from 10 to 240 min** (Fig. 3; end labels 67 / 69 / 9 / 11 / 22 / 20 for C1 / C2 / C3 / C4 / C5 / C6). Across conditions (Fig. 4 = Davidek 2006a Table 2): C-1/C-2 ~70 %, C-5/C-6 ~18 %, C-3/C-4 < 8 %; at 90 °C more from C-5/C-6 (~25 % at pH 6) and less from C-3/C-4 (~5 %) | [M] / [F] |

**Answer.** On the question that matters for B7a-2 -- does an amine accelerate the deoxyosone beta-cleavage? -- this
paper is **silent**: no precursor was heated with and without amine, and no 1-DG pot was run at all (the 1-DG
experiments are "reported elsewhere", i.e. Davidek 2006a). Confidence that nothing in it answers amine acceleration:
**~95 %**. What it adds:

1. **The DFG numbers are now sourced.** 4 / 28 / 56 mol % are 240-min end labels of a measured 120 °C, phosphate,
   pH 4 / 6 / 8 time course (5 / 3 / 3 markers at pH 8 / 6 / 4), quantified by the same SIDA as Davidek 2006a Table 1.
   The Fru-Gly concentration is not printed [!]; 0.1 M is inferred (~85 %).
2. **Consistency with the amine-free 1-DG branching [Z].** If every acetic acid passes through 1-DG (Davidek 2006a's
   mechanism; Fig. 4 here: all six carbons, C-1/C-2 dominant) and the per-1-DG yield with liberated glycine equals the
   amine-free one (Davidek 2006a Fig. 3, 60 min: 0.56 at pH 6, 0.80-0.84 at pH 8), then **>= 50 % (pH 6) and
   >= 67-70 % (pH 8) of DFG decomposes via 2,3-enolisation to 1-DG**. Plausible, so the DFG yields are compatible with
   NO amine acceleration; they are equally compatible with acceleration plus a smaller 1-DG share. Not separable.
3. **The pH 6 -> 8 rise is steeper from DFG (x2.0) than from 1-DG without amine (x1.46 at 60 min) [Z].** The excess
   (x1.37) must sit upstream of the cleavage (DFG's 2,3-enolisation share and rate rising with pH, as Davidek 2002
   saw at 90 °C) or in an amine effect on the cleavage. For the engine: a saturating cleavage law (B7AS, flat above
   ~pH 6.5) is **not contradicted** by the DFG / glucose pots, provided the AMA -> ODG partition (or the pentose
   enolisation split) carries the remaining pH 6 -> 8 rise. Confidence the saturating law survives these rows:
   ~70 % (residual risk: the in-pot pH drifts down as up to ~56 mM acid forms in 0.2 M phosphate [Z], so the pH 8
   pot spends time nearer pH 7).
4. **The acid side is steep.** pH 4 -> 6: DFG x7, glucose x17 [Z]. A saturating law with pK ~6 gives a cleavage
   factor ~0.18 at pH 5 vs 1 at pH 6 (prereg sec. 13 note), the direction these rows need; the glucose pots add the
   condensation step's own pH law, so only DFG isolates the post-Amadori chain.
5. **Fast DFG kinetics at 120 °C [F/Z].** At pH 8, ~75 % of the 240-min Fru-Gly yield is reached by 15 min and ~90 %
   by 30 min; at pH 6 ~70 % by 30 min. The 4 h plateau reflects DFG exhaustion, so the plateau ratio is a branching
   ratio, not a rate.
6. **Hexose, not pentose.** All pots are glucose-derived: they inform the engine's AMA -> ODG -> AA chain
   (`r_ama_odg`, `r_odg_aa`), and the pentose DPO cleavage (`r_dpo_aa`, the B7a-2 target) only by analogy (~75 %, as in
   davidek2006a_extraction.md).

## 3. Methods [M]

| experiment | as printed |
|---|---|
| Glucose / glycine | glycine 0.35 mmol + D-glucose (or [1-13C] ... [6-13C]glucose, 99 %) 0.35 mmol in phosphate buffer (3.5 mL, 0.2 mol/L; NaH2PO4 / Na2HPO4, Merck), 0.4 mL per 1.5 mL screw-cap vial (Infochroma), silicone bath, 120 °C "for a defined period of time"; pH 4, 6, 8. Results: "equimolar concentrations ... (0.1 mol/L)" |
| 13C runs | "at two temperatures (90°C and 120°C) at pH 6 and 8" (Fig. 4 legend: 90 °C 15 h, 120 °C 4 h); the Methods mention only 120 °C [!] |
| **Fru-Gly** | synthesised per Staempfli 1994 (ref 8). **No pot description**: only "When glucose and glycine were replaced by corresponding Amadori compound Fru-Gly, a similar effect was observed" (Results) [!] |
| 3-DG / glycine | glycine 0.05 mmol + 3-deoxyglucos-2-ulose (Toronto Research Chemicals) 0.05 mmol in phosphate buffer (0.5 mL, 0.2 mol/L) -> 0.1 M each, 1.5 mL screw-cap vial, 120 °C, 4 h; pH 4, 6, 8 |
| Acetic acid | IDA with [2H3]acetic acid (Isotec): aliquot spiked, acidified with H3PO4 (85 %), SPME (PDMS-DVB, 30 min at 25 °C, headspace), desorbed 5 min at 250 °C; GC 6890A / MSD 5973, DB-Wax 30 m x 0.25 mm x 0.25 µm, 20 -> 240 °C at 6 °C/min; EI 70 eV; m/z 60 (analyte) / 63 (standard) |
| Formic acid | **method not described** [!] (Davidek 2006a: quantified against [2H3]acetic acid, not SIDA) |
| Replicates / errors | none stated; Fig. 4 carries error bars (undefined); Figs. 1, 3 none |

**Fig. 1, acetic acid (mol % of glucose or of Fru-Gly), 120 °C, phosphate.** End labels at 240 min printed [M]; other
points read by me from an 800 dpi render, gridlines 0 / 25 / 50 / 75 / 100 (~24 px per mol %), marker centres,
read error ~ +-0.5 mol %. Glucose / glycine columns checked against Davidek 2006a Table 1 (in parentheses): every
read within 0.4 mol %, so the glucose series here IS that table.

| min | Glc+Gly pH 4 | Glc+Gly pH 6 | Glc+Gly pH 8 | Fru-Gly pH 4 | Fru-Gly pH 6 | Fru-Gly pH 8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 15 | no marker | **~6.6** (ND in 2006a) | ~21.2 (21.4) | no marker | no marker | ~42 |
| 30 | no marker | ~9.7 (9.7) | ~28.2 (28.3) | no marker | ~20.0 | ~50.2 |
| 60 | ~0.2 (0.28) | ~12.5 (12.6) | ~33.0 (33.0) | ~1.7 | ~25.5 | ~53.3 |
| 120 | ~0.5 (0.48) | ~14.8 (15.1) | ~37.4 (37.0) | ~2.8 | no marker; the dotted line bends at ~27 [!] | ~54.5 |

t = 0 markers at 0 for all series. Davidek 2006a's 480-min pH 4 cell is not plotted here.

**Table 1 (3-DG + glycine, 120 °C, 4 h):** acetic acid 0.8 / 1.5 / 2.4, formic acid 0.9 / 1.5 / 1.7 at pH 4 / 6 / 8,
header "(mol/mol 3-DG)" [M] -- a unit misprint, see section 5. Authors: the 1,2-enolisation pathway "does not
contribute significantly" to acetic acid; formic acid "low and comparable to those of acetic acid", so alpha-cleavage
of 3-DG "cannot be considered as a major pathway" to formic acid [Q].

**Fig. 3 (120 °C, pH 8, % singly labelled acetic acid vs time, 10 / 20 / 30 / 60 / 120 / 240 min):** flat lines; end
labels C-2 69, C-1 67, C-5 22, C-6 20, C-4 11, C-3 9 [M]; 10-min points ~65-69 (C1/C2), ~18-20 (C5/C6), ~9-11
(C3/C4) [F]. Sum of the six end labels 198 % ~ 200 % (two carbons per acetic acid) [Z]: internally consistent.
y-axis titled "Yield (mol%)" although the quantity is a label share [!].

**Fig. 4 (four conditions):** bar heights match Davidek 2006a Table 2 (e.g. C-1 at 90 °C pH 6 ~69, C-4 at 120 °C pH 8
~11, C-5 at 90 °C pH 6 ~25) [F]; the numbers are taken from 2006a Table 2, not re-read here.

**Mechanism (Fig. 2) [Q]:** A, alpha-dicarbonyl cleavage of 1-deoxyhexo-2,3-diulose (the literature route,
refs Brands 2001, Hodge 1953); B, alpha-cleavage of 3-DG -> formic acid; C, **beta-dicarbonyl cleavage of
1-deoxyhexo-2,4-diulose after isomerisation**, proposed as the major route ("experiments confirming this hypothesis
were done and will be reported elsewhere" = Davidek 2006a). No oxidant, no amine appears in scheme C.

Fru-Gly at 120 °C vs 90 °C: "final yields ... at 120°C were comparable to those obtained at 90°C" (citing Davidek 2002)
[Q/C].

## 5. Flags

- [!] **No amine on / off pair** on any precursor; no 1-DG pot. Question (a) is unanswered here.
- [!] **Fru-Gly pots undocumented**: concentration, buffer, volume not printed. Simulating them requires a declared
  assumption (0.1 M Fru-Gly, 0.2 M phosphate, 0.4 mL vial, no free glycine at t = 0).
- [!] **Table 1 unit misprint (~95 %).** The header says "mol/mol 3-DG"; Davidek 2006a prints the same numbers as
  "mol %", and the text here calls them "only small amounts" and "low" -- 2.4 mol acetic acid per mol 3-DG would be
  near-total conversion. `data/lit/fit_rows/ph_acid_davidek_acids.yml` keys them as mol % (0.8 mmol/L at 0.1 M 3-DG):
  correct; do not re-key from this paper.
- [!] Fru-Gly pH 6 has no 120-min marker (the line bends there at ~27 mol %); pH 4 has none before 60 min; pH 6 none
  at 15 min.
- [!] Fig. 3 y-axis label "Yield (mol%)" is a label share; Fig. 4 bars carry undefined error bars.
- Duplicates (count once): Fig. 1 glucose / glycine = Davidek 2006a Table 1 (keyed there); Fig. 4 = Davidek 2006a
  Table 2; Table 1 = Davidek 2006a 3-DG text (keyed there). New in this paper: the Fru-Gly time courses (Fig. 1),
  the glucose pH 6 15-min point (~6.6 mol %), the label shares vs time (Fig. 3).

|---|---|
| **Fig. 1 Fru-Gly series** (11 markers: pH 8 x5, pH 6 x3, pH 4 x3; the three 240-min values printed as labels) | **Key by two readers as a HOLD-OUT** for the engine's AMA -> ODG -> AA chain (`r_ama_odg`, `r_odg_aa`; species AMA exists) at 120 °C and pH 4 / 6 / 8. Not a fit row: the concentration is an assumption, the AMA rates come from Martins' network and the Davidek 2002 90 °C pots, and these are the only DFG acetic-acid pH series at 120 °C in the Davidek corpus, so they test temperature and pH extrapolation honestly. If the readers refuse figure reads, key only the three printed end labels (4 / 28 / 56 at 240 min). Pot fields: `initial_mmol_L: {AMA: 100.0}` declared as assumption, buffer "phosphate 0.2 M (inferred); pH not held" |
| Fig. 1 glucose / glycine | do not key (duplicate of Davidek 2006a Table 1); the extra pH 6 15-min point (~6.6) is optional, low value |

| Figs. 3 / 4 (13C shares) | not fit rows (the engine does not track isotopomers); Fig. 3's time-invariance is a mechanism check: one acetic-acid source family dominates at all times |
